# Droid Vault 3.0.1

## Fixed in this release

- **Headings no longer render in the accent blue.** Every card, sheet and dialog
  in the app was drawing its title in the link colour instead of the reading
  colour — so "Back up apps", "Backup Configurations" and every other navigation
  title looked like a hyperlink. Fixed in both dark and light themes.

## 3.0.0 — the UI release

3.0.0 was withdrawn shortly after publication because of the heading colour
above. Everything it introduced is below and is in this release.

A UI pass from end to end. Nothing about what Droid Vault backs up or restores
has changed.

### Text and colour

- The whole app now reads from one type scale; seven of the fifteen text styles
  had never been defined and fell back to the defaults.
- No text got bigger or smaller — headings lighter, titles bolder, nothing
  reflows.
- Droid Vault's own colours are now the default; your wallpaper palette is still
  in Settings → Theme.

### Large text

- The bottom bar no longer cuts the last letter off "Migrate".
- Home button names are no longer truncated to "Back up a...".
- The backup-health line keeps its ending, which is the part that tells you what
  to do about it.

### Spacing and touch

- The empty band across the middle of the Home screen is gone; the shortcut
  editor moved into the top bar.
- Small buttons are now big enough to hit — they were 28–40dp against a 48dp
  minimum, and looked small only because their icons were.
- Action chips wrap instead of scrolling sideways with names that flashed past.
- Advice that names an action is no longer truncated mid-verb.

### Motion

- Every animation now shares one set of timings; there were fourteen.
- A spinner can no longer look like it stopped mid-turn.

### Manage Backups

- New Device data card: every device archive with its size, date and health, and
  a delete that goes through the recoverable trash.
- A row can no longer claim your vault is empty because a read failed.
- Export deletes moved here, so destructive actions live in one place.

### Import and export

- Both now ask first, and say what will happen.
- The sheet states the size, the space needed, where files go, and that your
  existing backups are kept and nothing is overwritten.
- "Find it somewhere else…" asks too — it was the one way in with nothing said.
- Exporting asks too, and the one-file-or-parts choice moved into that sheet.
- A split now says *why* it needs twice the room instead of quoting a number
  that looks like a bug.
- Exports show their size as the headline and an Import button, with a dot
  saying whether each is actually restorable.
- With no exports, the Import page tells you what's true about your backups.

### Diagnostics

- The log now records what actually happened — counts, names, sizes — and names
  the archive a finding is about instead of reporting a bare count.
- The Live log filters by severity, searches, and keeps your scroll position
  when you scroll up to read.
- The status line says what each number is.
- Copy on an empty log no longer claims it copied one line.

### Icons

- "Back up device data" and "Restore device data" wore the same picture; they
  are different now.
- "Erase Native" wore a phone-settings icon.

## Upgrading

Your backup folder is untouched. Install over your existing copy — your
settings, labels, app assignments, configurations and scheduled jobs are kept.

If you installed 3.0.0, this replaces it directly.

## Download

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `arm64-v8a-release.apk` | Almost all phones from 2017 onward |
| `armeabi-v7a-release.apk` | Older 32-bit phones |

Not sure? Take the 64-bit one.

**Needs** a rooted device (Magisk, KernelSU or APatch) and Android 10+.

Please keep a second backup somewhere else.
